title: University of Fort Hare RCDI-Nested Scholarships & Postdoctoral Research Fellowship 2026: Fully Funded Master’s, PhD, and Postdoctoral Opportunities in Industrial & Organisational Psychology (South Africa)
summary: Researchers and aspiring postgraduate students interested in occupational health, workplace safety, organisational psychology, and nursing research now have an exciting opportunity to advance their academic and research careers through the University of Fort Hare RCDI-Nested Scholarship and Fellowship Programme 2026 . The University of Fort Hare is inviting applications for RCDI-Nested Master s Scholarships, PhD Scholarships, and Postdoctoral Research Fellowships under a research project focused on The Management of Workplace Violence and Injury on the Outcomes of Work: The Role of Decent Work and Workplace Safety Amongst Nurses in South Africa. These prestigious opportunities provide substantial annual funding for eligible South African Master s students, PhD candidates, and early-career postdoctoral researchers interested in conducting research in Industrial and Organisational Psychology . The programme particularly encourages applications from women, persons with disabilities, and candidates from historically disadvantaged groups. Applications close on 15 August 2026 . About the RCDI-Nested Programme The RCDI-Nested funding opportunities are hosted by the University of Fort Hare and support research under a broader project investigating workplace violence, occupational injuries, workplace safety, and decent work among nurses in South Africa. The research aims to generate evidence that contributes to improving workplace conditions and employee wellbeing within the healthcare sector while advancing knowledge in Industrial and Organisational Psychology. The funding is released after all required agreements have been signed between: South African Medical Research Council (SAMRC) Host Institution (HDI) Principal Investigator (PI) Successful student or fellow Funding renewal is also dependent on satisfactory academic or research progress and continued funding availability. Research Project Focus All applicants will undertake research aligned with the following project: The Management of Workplace Violence and Injury on the Outcomes of Work: The Role of Decent Work and Workplace Safety Amongst Nurses in South Africa Applicants are expected to prepare research proposals that clearly align with this research theme. Available Opportunities The programme offers funding under three separate categories: RCDI-Nested Master s Scholarship RCDI-Nested PhD Scholarship RCDI-Nested Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Each category has different funding levels, duration, and eligibility requirements. 1. RCDI-Nested Master s Scholarship The Master s Scholarship supports students pursuing postgraduate research in Industrial and Organisational Psychology . Scholarship Value Successful candidates will receive: R200,000 per year Duration Funding is available for: Up to 2 years (maximum) Funding renewal each year depends on: Satisfactory progress reports Availability of funding Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be South African citizens or permanent residents. Be registered or intending to register for a Master s degree in Industrial and Organisational Psychology. Demonstrate academic readiness for postgraduate research. The University also notes that: Individuals with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Preference will be given to candidates from historically disadvantaged groups. Full-time employees may not hold an RCDI-Nested Master s Scholarship. 2. RCDI-Nested PhD Scholarship The PhD Scholarship supports doctoral candidates conducting research in Industrial and Organisational Psychology. Scholarship Value Successful candidates will receive: R250,000 per year Duration Funding is available for: 3 years An additional year may be approved upon motivation. Funding renewal depends on: Satisfactory annual progress Availability of funding Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be South African citizens or permanent residents. Be registered or intending to register for a PhD in Industrial and Organisational Psychology. The University further indicates: Persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Preference will be given to candidates from historically disadvantaged groups. Full-time employees may not hold an RCDI-Nested PhD Scholarship. 3. RCDI-Nested Postdoctoral Research Fellowship The Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed for early-career researchers who have recently completed a PhD. Fellowship Value Successful fellows will receive: R350,000 per year Fellowship Duration Appointments are made for: One year initially The fellowship may be renewed: For up to three years Renewal depends on: Satisfactory performance Availability of funding Work Commitment Selected fellows will be expected to devote: 80% of their time to the RCDI research project. 20% of their time to career development activities. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must: Be South African citizens or permanent residents. Be younger than 40 years . Applicants older than 40 years may still be nominated if supported by a strong motivation from the Principal Investigator. Additional requirements include: Applicants must be within five years of completing their PhD . Preference is given to applicants whose doctoral research is in: Social Science Health Medical-related research The proposed research must form part of the funded RCDI project. The University also notes: Women are encouraged to apply. Persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Preference will be given to candidates from historically disadvantaged groups. Full-time employees may not hold an RCDI-Nested Postdoctoral Fellowship. Funding Summary Opportunity Funding Duration Master s Scholarship R200,000 per year Up to 2 years PhD Scholarship R250,000 per year 3 years (plus possible extension) Postdoctoral Fellowship R350,000 per year Renewable annually for up to 3 years Required Application Documents Applicants should submit: Curriculum Vitae (CV) Academic qualifications Motivation letter Proposed concept note related to the research project The concept note should clearly explain: The research gap Proposed research design Alignment with the project theme Where to Submit Applications Applications should be submitted to: Prof Willie Chinyamurindi Email: wchinyamurindi@ufh.ac.za Application Deadline Deadline: 15 August 2026 Applicants are encouraged to prepare all required documents early to avoid missing the submission deadline. Why Apply? These RCDI-Nested opportunities offer far more than financial support. Successful applicants will benefit from: Generous annual research funding. Opportunity to conduct research on a nationally important healthcare issue. Supervision within a funded research project. Academic development in Industrial and Organisational Psychology. Research experience focused on workplace safety and occupational health. Opportunity to contribute evidence that may influence workplace policy and employee wellbeing. Career advancement in academia and research. For postdoctoral fellows, the structured career development component provides additional opportunities to strengthen research and professional skills while contributing to high-impact scholarship. Who Should Consider Applying? This programme is particularly suitable for: Honours graduates progressing to Master s study. Master s graduates planning doctoral research. Recent PhD graduates pursuing postdoctoral research. Researchers interested in occupational health and safety. Industrial and Organisational Psychology researchers. Scholars interested in workplace violence and employee wellbeing. Early-career academics seeking funded research opportunities. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) What research topic will successful applicants work on? All successful applicants will undertake research aligned with the project: The Management of Workplace Violence and Injury on the Outcomes of Work: The Role of Decent Work and Workplace Safety Amongst Nurses in South Africa. How much funding is available? Funding varies by programme: Master s: R200,000 per year PhD: R250,000 per year Postdoctoral Fellowship: R350,000 per year Can full-time employees apply? According to the programme information, full-time employees may not hold these RCDI-Nested awards . Are persons with disabilities encouraged to apply? Yes. Individuals with disabilities are specifically encouraged to submit applications. Is preference given to any applicants? Yes. Preference will be given to applicants from historically disadvantaged groups. Women are also specifically encouraged to apply for the Postdoctoral Fellowship. What documents are required? Applicants should submit: CV Academic qualifications Motivation letter Proposed concept note Who should receive applications? Applications should be emailed to: Prof Willie Chinyamurindi Email: wchinyamurindi@ufh.ac.za When is the application deadline? Applications must be submitted by: 15 August 2026 Visit HERE to learn more about the University of Fort Hare RCDI-Nested Scholarships Postdoctoral Research Fellowship 2026. Conclusion The University of Fort Hare RCDI-Nested Master s Scholarships, PhD Scholarships, and Postdoctoral Research Fellowship 2026 provide exceptional opportunities for South African postgraduate students and early-career researchers committed to advancing knowledge in Industrial and Organisational Psychology. Through generous annual funding, participants will contribute to an important research project examining workplace violence, occupational injury, decent work, and workplace safety among nurses in South Africa. Whether you are preparing for a Master s degree, pursuing doctoral research, or seeking to strengthen your academic career through postdoctoral research, these opportunities offer substantial financial support and the chance to contribute to research with real-world significance. Eligible applicants are encouraged to prepare their application documents, develop a strong concept note aligned with the project focus, and submit their applications before the 15 August 2026 deadline. Discover more global Scholarship , Research , Fellowship , and African opportunities on OFY. title: Energy Communities Leadership Seminar Powering Change for Rural Youth in Europe
summary: Introduction: Rural Youth and the Energy Transition The energy transition in Europe is one of the most ambitious societal transformations of our time. It is not only about shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources but also about rethinking how communities organize, govern, and sustain themselves. At the heart of this transformation lies the concept of energy communities — local, citizen‑led initiatives that empower people to take control of their energy future. Rural areas, often marginalized in national policy debates, are uniquely positioned to benefit from and contribute to this transition. They are rich in renewable resources such as wind, solar, and biomass, yet they face persistent challenges: limited infrastructure, energy poverty, geographic isolation, and reduced political influence. These challenges can make rural communities feel excluded from the broader energy transition. However, rural youth represent a powerful force for change. They are deeply connected to their communities, understand local realities, and bring creativity, resilience, and innovation to problem‑solving. Yet, many lack access to the training, networks, and resources necessary to lead energy initiatives. Without targeted support, their potential remains untapped. This is where Rural Youth Europe (RYE) steps in. Through the Powering Change – Empowering Rural Youth for Energy Communities project , RYE is committed to equipping young people with the knowledge, skills, and partnerships needed to establish and support local energy communities. The flagship event of this initiative is the Capacity‑Building Seminar on Energy Communities , scheduled for 1–4 November 2026 in Bilbao, Spain . This seminar is not just another conference. It is a transformative experience designed to empower 25 motivated young participants from across Europe. Over three days, they will learn from experts, engage in interactive workshops, and collaborate with peers to explore the practical aspects of developing energy communities in rural areas. The seminar will strengthen their capacity to become local leaders of the energy transition, capable of building community‑led energy initiatives that are sustainable, inclusive, and impactful. About the Seminar The seminar is designed as an immersive, multi‑day experience where participants move beyond theory into practice. Dates: 1–4 November 2026 Location: Bilbao, Spain — a city known for innovation and sustainability. Organizers: Rural Youth Europe (RYE), a network dedicated to empowering rural youth. Participants: 25 selected young people from diverse European countries and rural contexts. The seminar will blend expert lectures with interactive workshops, peer learning, and collaborative project design. Participants will explore governance models, financing strategies, technical solutions, and community engagement approaches. The emphasis is on practical application — equipping participants with tools they can take back to their communities. Objectives of the Seminar Knowledge Development Provide a comprehensive overview of energy communities, their role in Europe’s energy transition, and the unique challenges faced by rural areas. Explore European policy frameworks supporting community energy initiatives. Skill Building Train participants in project management, stakeholder engagement, and technical planning. Offer hands‑on exercises in designing energy community models. Networking and Partnerships Facilitate connections among participants, experts, and practitioners. title: PhD Position in Urban Health Equity 2026: Heat Risks, Pediatric Respiratory Health and Greenspace Interventions at the University of Amsterdam
summary: Introduction: Climate Change, Urban Health, and Equity Climate change is not a distant abstraction; it is a lived reality shaping the daily experiences of millions of people across the globe. Cities, as hubs of human activity, are particularly vulnerable to its impacts. The urban heat island effect intensifies heat waves, raising temperatures in built environments far above those in surrounding rural areas. This phenomenon is compounded by environmental degradation, air pollution, and socio‑economic inequalities, creating a perfect storm of health risks. Children are among the most vulnerable groups in this context. Their respiratory systems are still developing, making them highly sensitive to pollutants, aeroallergens, and extreme heat exposure. Research consistently shows that heat events correlate with increased asthma rates, exacerbations of chronic respiratory conditions, and long‑term reductions in lung function. These health challenges do not exist in isolation; they ripple outward, influencing educational achievement, social participation, and future socio‑economic attainment. The University of Amsterdam (UvA) has recognized the urgency of addressing these interconnected challenges. Through its Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences, UvA is offering a PhD position focused on Urban Health Equity and the Impacts of Heat Risks . This project is not merely academic; it is a call to action. By bridging biomedical sciences and urban studies, the research will explore how rising temperatures intersect with pediatric respiratory health and how urban greenspace interventions can serve as a pathway toward health equity. This PhD position is embedded in a broader vision: to understand the lived realities of marginalized urban populations, to connect scientific evidence with socio‑political contexts, and to generate actionable insights that can inform urban planning and public health policy. It is an opportunity to contribute to cutting‑edge interdisciplinary research that has both local relevance in Amsterdam Southeast and global significance in the fight for climate justice and health equity. Project Overview: Urban Greenspaces and Health Urban greenspaces are increasingly recognized as vital components of climate adaptation strategies. Parks, gardens, and green corridors can reduce local temperatures, improve air quality, and provide psychological and social benefits. Yet, the relationship between greenspaces and health is far from straightforward. Unequal distribution : Greenspaces are often concentrated in affluent neighborhoods, leaving marginalized communities with limited access. This unequal distribution perpetuates health disparities. Historical disinvestment : Many urban planning decisions have systematically neglected disadvantaged districts, amplifying inequities. Amsterdam Southeast, for example, has faced decades of underinvestment, making it a critical site for examining how new greenspaces can reshape health outcomes. Climate vs. health planning : Greenspaces are often designed to mitigate climate risks, such as reducing heat, but they do not automatically translate into improved health outcomes. The challenge lies in aligning climate adaptation strategies with public health goals. This PhD project will explore these dynamics in depth, focusing on Amsterdam Southeast and the newly created Nelson Mandelapark . By combining biomedical explanations (individual interactions with the environment as causes of disease) with urban political ecological explanations (socio‑political conditions shaping environments and institutions), the research will provide a holistic understanding of how greenspaces can promote health equity. Research Objectives The PhD candidate will undertake a series of interconnected research tasks designed to capture the complexity of urban health equity: Quantitative Vulnerability and Risk Assessment Map hydro‑meteorologic and pediatric respiratory health risks. Use intersectionality as a lens to understand how social identities (such as race, class, and gender) shape heat risk experiences. Combine mechanistic pathway mapping (secondary data on environmental stressors and respiratory outcomes) with qualitative interviews to capture lived experiences. Qualitative Examination of Urban Greenspace Planning Investigate dominant planning and management regimes. Conduct interviews with caregivers, residents, and public officials to understand how greening strategies intersect with health and climate change adaptation. Explore how policies and institutions shape access to greenspaces. Integrated Multi‑Scalar Analysis Link bodily experiences of heat exposure with political‑economic systems. Examine how urban environments shape pediatric respiratory health at multiple scales, from individual bodies to citywide planning regimes. Ranking and Prioritization of Greenspace Interventions Assess existing interventions in Amsterdam Southeast. Provide recommendations for future urban planning strategies that prioritize health equity. This multi‑layered approach ensures that the research captures both the biological mechanisms of disease and the socio‑political contexts that shape health outcomes. Supervisors and Institutional Context The PhD candidate will be supervised by: Dr Jannes Willems (Urban Planning, Department of Geography, Planning and International Development Studies) Dr Vanessa Harris (Department of Global Health, Amsterdam University Medical Centers) Prof Maria Kaika (Urban Studies and Political Ecology) The candidate will be embedded in the Urban Planning research group at UvA and affiliated with the Department of Global Health at Amsterdam UMC . This dual affiliation ensures a truly interdisciplinary environment, combining social science and biomedical expertise. Candidate Requirements Applicants should hold a (Research) Master’s degree in one or more of the following fields: Human geography Urban and regional planning Urban studies Public health Global health Medicine (MD) Biomedical sciences Environmental studies Interdisciplinary programs bridging these fields Preferred qualifications include: Experience conducting fieldwork in unfamiliar settings, demonstrating adaptability and resilience. Familiarity with mixed methods research, combining qualitative and quantitative approaches. Strong writing skills and ability to develop complex, critical arguments. Excellent English proficiency (written and verbal). Dutch language skills (preferred, for fieldwork in Amsterdam Southeast). Ability to work independently while also contributing to collaborative research teams. The ideal candidate will be passionate about interdisciplinary research, committed to social justice, and eager to contribute to innovative solutions at the intersection of climate adaptation, public health, and urban equity. Benefits and Opportunities Successful candidates will enjoy a range of benefits and opportunities: Interdisciplinary supervision : A supportive team of supervisors from both social science and biomedical backgrounds. International research networks : Opportunities to attend conferences, workshops, and seminars, connecting with scholars worldwide. Resources for fieldwork : Funding and logistical support for conducting research in Amsterdam Southeast. Professional development : Access to courses and training through the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research. Collaborative environment : Embedding in two leading research groups (Urban Planning and Global Health) that value curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking. This combination of resources and support ensures that the PhD candidate can thrive academically while also contributing to meaningful societal change. Application Process Applications must include: Curriculum vitae (with contact details for two references). Motivation letter (max 750 words), outlining your interest in the project and your suitability for the role. Research statement (max 500 words), sharing your initial ideas on how to approach the project. Writing sample in English (article, thesis chapter, or assignment). Deadline: Applications close on 9 August 2026 . Interviews: Week of 7 September 2026 (preferably in person in Amsterdam). Start date: 1 November 2026. For inquiries, contact: Dr Jannes Willems (j.j.willems@uva.nl) Dr Vanessa Harris (v.c.harris@amsterdamumc.nl) Apply HERE today! FAQs 1. What is the central focus of this PhD project? The project investigates how rising temperatures and environmental degradation affect pediatric respiratory health, particularly in marginalized urban communities. It also explores how urban greenspace interventions can mitigate these impacts. The research is designed to connect biomedical explanations (individual interactions with the environment as causes of disease) with urban political ecological explanations (socio‑political conditions shaping environments and institutions). 2. Where will the research be conducted? Fieldwork will take place in Amsterdam Southeast , with a particular focus on the newly created Nelson Mandelapark . This location is significant because it represents both a site of new greenspace development and a community that has historically faced socio‑economic challenges. 3. What disciplines are relevant for applicants? Applicants from a wide range of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including human geography, urban and regional planning, urban studies, public health, global health, medicine, biomedical sciences, and environmental studies. Interdisciplinary backgrounds that bridge these fields are especially valued. 4. Is Dutch language proficiency required? While Dutch proficiency is not mandatory, it is highly preferred. Fieldwork will involve engaging with caregivers, residents, and public officials in Amsterdam Southeast, many of whom may be more comfortable communicating in Dutch. Having this skill will enhance the depth and authenticity of the research. 5. What is the application deadline? Applications close on 9 August 2026 . This deadline is firm, and candidates are encouraged to prepare their materials well in advance to ensure timely submission. 6. When will interviews be held? Interviews are scheduled for the week of 7 September 2026 , preferably in person in Amsterdam. This provides an opportunity for candidates to meet the supervision team and gain a deeper understanding of the research environment. 7. What is the expected start date? The preferred start date is 1 November 2026 . This allows sufficient time for onboarding, preparation, and integration into the research groups at UvA and Amsterdam UMC. 8. What kind of support will the PhD candidate receive? The candidate will benefit from an enthusiastic and warm interdisciplinary supervision team, access to international research networks, resources for fieldwork, and professional development opportunities through the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research. 9. How does this project contribute to broader societal goals? By focusing on pediatric respiratory health and greenspace interventions, the project addresses urgent societal challenges related to climate adaptation, public health, and social justice. The findings will have implications not only for Amsterdam but also for cities worldwide grappling with similar issues. To learn more about the PhD Position Urban Health Equity click HERE. Conclusion This PhD position at the University of Amsterdam is more than an academic opportunity; it is a chance to contribute to transformative research at the intersection of climate change, urban health, and equity. The project recognizes that children are at the frontline of climate impacts, and that their health outcomes are deeply intertwined with socio‑economic conditions and urban environments. By investigating how rising temperatures and environmental degradation affect pediatric respiratory health, and by exploring the potential of greenspace interventions, the research aims to generate actionable insights that can inform urban planning, public health policy, and climate adaptation strategies. The University of Amsterdam offers a supportive, interdisciplinary environment where curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking are valued. Candidates who are passionate about interdisciplinary research, committed to social justice, and eager to contribute to innovative solutions are strongly encouraged to apply. The deadline for applications is 9 August 2026 , with interviews scheduled for the week of 7 September 2026 and a preferred start date of 1 November 2026 . This timeline ensures that the selected candidate can begin their journey at UvA with clarity and purpose. In conclusion, this PhD position represents a unique opportunity to engage in research that is both academically rigorous and socially impactful. It is an invitation to join a community of scholars dedicated to addressing some of the most pressing challenges of our time, and to contribute to a vision of healthier, more equitable, and more resilient cities. The MSc in Global Plant Health prepares graduates to develop innovative scientific solutions that address these challenges through research, biotechnology, genetics, molecular biology, bioinformatics, and plant pathology. Graduates are expected to become leaders capable of improving agriculture both nationally and internationally. Scholarship Types Available 1. David Sainsbury Full MSc Scholarship The Full Scholarship is intended primarily for applicants from least-developed, low-income, and lower-middle-income countries. This scholarship covers nearly every major cost associated with studying in the UK. Benefits of the Full Scholarship Successful applicants may receive funding covering: Full tuition fees (up to £36,000 for the 2026/27 academic year) Monthly maintenance allowance (to be confirmed; based on the UKRI postgraduate stipend, which was £20,780 in 2025/26) Up to £4,000 for economy-class travel expenses upon submission of valid receipts Financial support for living costs throughout the programme Payments for tuition fees are made directly by The Sainsbury Laboratory to the University of East Anglia. Maintenance grants are paid monthly in advance to scholarship recipients. Travel reimbursements are processed after valid receipts are submitted. Full Scholarship Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy all of the following: Hold an offer of admission to the UEA MSc in Global Plant Health. Be a national of or permanently domiciled in a least-developed, low-income, or lower-middle-income country according to the applicable OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC) list. Successfully complete the admission interview. Meet all academic admission requirements. Submit a convincing Statement of Intent outlining plans to return to their home country within five years after graduation to contribute towards solving plant disease challenges. Commitment After Graduation Recipients of the Full Scholarship are expected to return to their country of origin within five years after completing their studies. Graduates are encouraged to contribute to: Agricultural development Scientific research Food security Plant disease management National economic development Community advancement The scholarship therefore represents both financial support and an investment in scientific development across low- and middle-income countries. 2. David Sainsbury 50% Fee Scholarship Applicants from upper-middle-income countries and high-income countries—including the United Kingdom—are automatically considered for the David Sainsbury 50% Fee Scholarship. Benefits of the 50% Fee Scholarship Recipients receive: 50% reduction of tuition fees Tuition support for either Home or International tuition rates Direct payment of scholarship funds to the University For the 2026/27 academic year, the scholarship covers: 50% of the £16,000 Home tuition fee, or 50% of the £36,000 International tuition fee Any existing scholarships exceeding 50% of tuition may affect the value of this award. Eligibility for the 50% Fee Scholarship Applicants must: Hold an offer for the MSc in Global Plant Health. Be from an upper-middle-income or high-income country. Meet all admission requirements. Successfully complete the interview process. Submit the required Statement of Intent after receiving an offer. How Scholarship Selection Works There is no separate scholarship application . Every eligible applicant who applies for admission to the MSc programme before the admission deadline published by UEA is automatically considered. The scholarship selection process includes: Submission of the MSc application to UEA. Academic evaluation. Interview. Formal offer of admission. Submission of a Statement of Intent. Review by the Scholarship Selection Panel. Scholarship offer to successful applicants. Selection Criteria Scholarships are awarded based on several factors, including: Academic excellence Previous academic awards Scientific knowledge Research experience Laboratory skills Understanding of molecular biology Genetics Plant health research Molecular interactions Bioinformatics Statistics Independent research ability Overall potential to contribute to solving plant disease challenges The Statement of Intent also plays a significant role in determining scholarship recipients. Statement of Intent Requirements Eligible applicants will be invited to prepare a written Statement of Intent. Applicants from low- and middle-income countries must explain: How they intend to return home after graduation. How they will use their education to address plant diseases. How they will contribute to scientific advancement and agriculture. Applicants from higher-income countries should describe: How they plan to contribute towards addressing plant disease challenges in low- and middle-income countries. Scholarship Expectations Successful scholars are expected to: Maintain excellent academic performance. Pass every module. Participate actively throughout the programme. Live within reasonable commuting distance of The Sainsbury Laboratory. Attend induction and welcome events. Maintain communication with TSL. Follow the TSL Scientific Integrity Policy. Follow the TSL Code of Personal Conduct. Remain in good financial standing with the University. Situations That May Lead to Scholarship Withdrawal The scholarship may be withdrawn if a student: Is expelled, suspended, or excluded. Provides false information. Commits fraud or dishonesty. Violates TSL ethics or integrity policies. Fails to attend required induction events. Demonstrates poor academic performance. Fails any module. Does not maintain financial obligations with the University. Receives undisclosed funding from another scholarship. Fails to cooperate with required scholarship communications. If withdrawn, recipients may be required to repay tuition fees, maintenance grants, and any other scholarship funds already received. Scholarship Deferral Policy Scholarship awards cannot be deferred . Applicants who postpone admission must compete again for scholarships available in the following academic year. Receiving a scholarship in one year does not guarantee funding in a later year. Marketing and Ambassador Responsibilities Scholarship recipients agree to participate in reasonable promotional activities organised by TSL and UEA. These activities may include: Student testimonials Interviews Photography Public speaking Blogging Social media participation Open Day events Supporting prospective students Recipients are also expected to complete a testimonial at the end of the programme explaining how the scholarship supported their career development. Scholarship Payment Schedule The scholarship is administered as follows: Tuition fees are paid directly to UEA by The Sainsbury Laboratory. Maintenance grants are paid monthly. Travel expenses are reimbursed upon submission of valid economy-class travel receipts. Tuition payments are generally made in three instalments during the academic year. Important Scholarship Conditions Applicants should note that: Scholarships are limited in number. Awards depend on available funding. The Scholarship Panel reserves the right not to make an award if no candidate meets the required standard. Scholarship terms may change before the application deadline provided applicants are not disadvantaged. Applicants remain responsible for paying tuition deposits and fees until a scholarship is officially awarded. Scholarship recipients must complete the University registration process by the required deadline. Acceptance of the scholarship requires signing and submitting the Scholarship Agreement Form before the specified acceptance deadline. Deadline Applicants must submit their application for admission to the MSc in Global Plant Health before the official application deadline published on the University of East Anglia website. The scholarship terms do not specify an exact application deadline. Since scholarship consideration is automatic, applicants are strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible because scholarships are limited and awarded competitively. To learn more about this opportunity and apply click HERE Conclusion The David Sainsbury International MSc Scholarships represent one of the leading opportunities for aspiring plant scientists who wish to develop advanced expertise in Global Plant Health while studying at one of the United Kingdom s respected research institutions. Whether through the fully funded scholarship for applicants from least-developed, low-income, and lower-middle-income countries or the 50% Fee Scholarship for applicants from higher-income countries, the programme is designed to develop highly skilled professionals capable of addressing plant diseases that threaten global agriculture and food security.With no separate scholarship application required, eligible students simply need to apply for admission to the MSc in Global Plant Health at the University of East Anglia before the official admissions deadline. Selection is based on academic excellence, scientific potential, interview performance, and a clear commitment to applying acquired knowledge to solve plant disease challenges worldwide. Applicants interested in this prestigious opportunity should prepare a strong application early, as scholarship places are limited and awarded on a competitive basis. title: UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026: Apply for Up to USD 30,000 to Strengthen Climate Resilience in East African Mountain Communities.
summary: Climate change continues to pose significant threats to mountain ecosystems and the millions of people who depend on them for water, agriculture, biodiversity, and sustainable livelihoods. To help local communities respond to these growing challenges, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) has officially opened the first Call for Proposals under the Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Project for 2026. This funding opportunity provides grants of up to USD 30,000 to eligible community-based organizations working in mountain regions across the East African Community (EAC). Through these grants, UNEP aims to empower local organizations to design and implement ecosystem-based adaptation initiatives that protect natural resources, strengthen climate resilience, and improve community livelihoods. Beyond financial support, selected organizations will also receive technical assistance, capacity development, and implementation training to ensure their projects achieve sustainable and measurable impacts. Applications are now open and must be submitted no later than 15 September 2026 at 11:59 PM East African Time (EAT). About the UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Project The Mountains ADAPT initiative is a UNEP-led project that promotes climate resilience in mountain regions through ecosystem-based adaptation and nature-based solutions. Mountain ecosystems are among the most vulnerable environments affected by climate change, making local adaptation initiatives increasingly important. The project recognizes that local organizations possess valuable knowledge of their communities and landscapes. By investing directly in community-led solutions, UNEP seeks to strengthen environmental conservation while improving the social and economic wellbeing of mountain populations. The first call for proposals focuses specifically on countries within the East African Community (EAC), where mountain communities are experiencing increasing climate-related risks such as: Drought Flooding Soil erosion Water scarcity Biodiversity loss Declining agricultural productivity Landslides Extreme weather events The project supports innovative solutions that not only address these challenges but also create long-term environmental and economic resilience. Grant Value Successful organizations may receive funding of up to: USD 30,000 There is no officially defined minimum funding amount. Applicants are encouraged to request a realistic budget that adequately supports meaningful project implementation. In addition to financial support, successful organizations will receive: Capacity development Technical guidance Project implementation training Institutional strengthening Monitoring and evaluation support Number of Projects to be Funded During this first funding round, UNEP plans to support: Up to 15 community-led projects across the East African Community. Objectives of the Small Grants Programme The Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Programme seeks to: Strengthen climate resilience in mountain communities. Promote ecosystem-based adaptation. Support community-driven environmental conservation. Protect mountain ecosystems. Improve local livelihoods. Encourage gender-inclusive climate action. Increase community ownership of adaptation projects. Enhance sustainable management of natural resources. Promote innovative nature-based solutions. Types of Projects That Can Be Funded Applicants are encouraged to develop practical, community-led projects that address local climate challenges through ecosystem-based adaptation. Examples of eligible interventions include: Ecosystem Restoration Projects may include: Forest restoration Indigenous tree planting Watershed rehabilitation Riverbank restoration Wetland conservation Soil restoration Water Management Potential activities include: Rainwater harvesting Spring protection Water conservation Community water infrastructure Sustainable watershed management Climate-Smart Agriculture Projects may support: Sustainable farming Agroforestry Improved irrigation Soil conservation Drought-resilient farming Sustainable food production Disaster Risk Reduction Organizations may propose activities such as: Community disaster preparedness Early warning systems Landslide prevention Flood mitigation Risk awareness campaigns Sustainable Livelihoods Projects may also include: Income diversification Green enterprises Community environmental businesses Sustainable natural resource management What Makes a Strong Proposal? UNEP encourages organizations to submit projects that: Respond to clearly identified climate risks. Demonstrate strong community ownership. Use ecosystem-based adaptation approaches. Integrate gender equality considerations. Promote youth participation where possible. Deliver measurable environmental and social benefits. Can be sustained beyond the grant period. Show innovation and potential for scaling up. What the Application Must Include Organizations are required to provide comprehensive information during the application process. 1. Organizational Information Applicants should provide: Organization name Registration details Registration number Organizational experience Previous projects Experience in mountain regions 2. Climate Challenge Applicants must explain: The climate risks affecting the community. Why the problem is significant. Visual evidence demonstrating the challenge. 3. Proposed Solution Organizations should describe: The planned intervention. How it addresses climate change. Ecosystem-based adaptation methods. Nature-based solutions. Gender-responsive approaches. Expected environmental outcomes. 4. Beneficiaries Applicants should identify: Target communities. Expected beneficiaries. Community participation. Long-term benefits. 5. Required Attachments Applicants must upload: Organization registration certificate. National ID or passport of the legal representative. Evidence of previous project experience. Who Can Apply? Eligible applicants include registered community organizations operating within mountain regions of eligible East African Community countries. Organizations should have demonstrated experience serving mountain communities and implementing environmental or climate-related initiatives. Eligible applicants include: Community-based organizations Grassroots organizations Civil society organizations Youth organizations Women-led organizations Registered NGOs Individuals are not eligible to apply. APPLY HERE. Countries Eligible for the Grant Organizations must be based in one of the following countries: Burundi Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Kenya Rwanda Somalia South Sudan Tanzania Uganda Required Organizational Experience Applicants should demonstrate: Previous work with mountain communities. Capacity to manage community projects. Knowledge of local environmental challenges. Experience implementing adaptation or environmental initiatives. Organizations do not need prior experience managing international donor funding. Required Documents Applicants must submit: Official registration certificate. National ID or passport of the legal representative. If selected, organizations must also provide: Official organizational bank account details. Eligible Project Costs Grant funding may be used for: Staff salaries Technical experts Equipment Project materials Community training Capacity-building activities Administrative costs Operational expenses Project implementation costs Funding Restrictions The grant cannot be used for: Direct salaries or allowances to government officials. Payments that fall outside the approved project scope. Government participation is encouraged through in-kind support or co-financing rather than direct grant payments. Is Co-Funding Required? No. Organizations are not required to secure co-funding. However, proposals with existing or anticipated financial support from municipalities or development partners may receive additional consideration during evaluation. Application Evaluation Process Applications will undergo several stages. Stage 1: Eligibility Screening Applications will first be reviewed to ensure: Eligibility requirements are met. Required documents are submitted. Application forms are complete. Stage 2: Technical Evaluation Eligible proposals will then be assessed by the Selection Committee using an official evaluation matrix. Key assessment criteria include: Relevance to climate challenges Technical feasibility Community participation Innovation Gender inclusion Youth inclusion Sustainability Environmental safeguards Potential for scaling up Stage 3: Final Selection Regional Selection Committees will select up to 15 successful projects. Click HERE for more information on UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants 2026. What Happens After Selection? Successful organizations will: Develop a detailed implementation plan. Prepare milestones and timelines. Receive organizational capacity assessments. Participate in technical training. Receive tailored implementation support. Begin project implementation. Reporting Requirements Successful organizations must submit: Mid-Term Report Including: Project progress Financial expenditure Supporting documentation Final Report Including: Final achievements Financial reporting Photos Videos Project evidence Some projects may also be selected for field monitoring visits. Project Timeline Key milestones include: Application deadline: 15 September 2026 (11:59 PM EAT) Notification of selected organizations: Third Quarter of 2026 Project implementation begins: Fourth Quarter of 2026 Grant implementation period: 12 months Languages Accepted Applications may be submitted in: English French Kiswahili How to Apply Interested organizations should: Complete the official online application form. Upload all required supporting documents. Submit the proposal before the deadline. Await eligibility screening. Respond to any requests for additional information if contacted. Wait for the regional selection process and notification. Need Assistance? Organizations requiring technical support or clarification during the application process may contact the UNEP Mountains ADAPT project team via: Email: unep-mountainsadapt@un.org Why Organizations Should Apply The Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Programme offers more than funding. It provides local organizations with an opportunity to strengthen institutional capacity, implement community-led climate solutions, and contribute to long-term environmental sustainability across East Africa s mountain ecosystems. Organizations will benefit from technical guidance, increased visibility, and practical experience implementing nature-based adaptation strategies that improve resilience for vulnerable communities. For organizations already working with mountain communities, this grant presents an excellent opportunity to expand their impact while contributing to regional climate adaptation goals. Conclusion The 2026 UNEP Mountains ADAPT Small Grants Programme is an important funding opportunity for community-based organizations dedicated to protecting mountain ecosystems and improving climate resilience across the East African Community. With grants of up to USD 30,000, comprehensive technical support, and a strong emphasis on ecosystem-based adaptation, the programme empowers local organizations to lead transformative environmental initiatives that benefit both people and nature. Eligible organizations are encouraged to prepare high-quality proposals that demonstrate strong community engagement, innovative climate solutions, and sustainable environmental outcomes. Interested applicants should ensure they submit all required documents before the 15 September 2026 deadline to be considered for this competitive funding opportunity. For more OFY Grant opportunities VISIT HERE.
